name: nginx2root
tile_line: Public exploit for HTTP/2. Same fix covers 9 more bugs.
tldr: An attacker with no login can crash nginx workers over HTTP/2 or run code as the worker user, not root. Public exploit out, no attacks seen. Upgrade nginx, above all if HTTP/2 is on; the same releases fix nine more bugs, some without HTTP/2.
summary: Despite the name, it doesn't give root by itself: Xint got root by chaining it with a separate Linux kernel bug, covered on our [Linux SCTP root](/linux-sctp-root/) page. F5 says running code needs ASLR off or bypassed; Rapid7's public exploit gets around ASLR with addresses the bug itself leaks, but it sends about 128 GB of HTTP/2 data and its README says it will likely fail against a server with several clients at once, while Xint says its own unreleased exploit worked under normal traffic against public servers on AWS, GCP and Azure. The nine other bugs fixed in the same 18 Nov releases include the four other bugs Xint reported as nginx2root (a second HTTP/2 bug, HTTP/3, resolver and mail proxy) and a TLS 1.3 hang; turning off HTTP/2 covers only the two HTTP/2 bugs.

affected.label: nginx before 1.31.9 / 1.30.7
affected.text: Stable 1.30.7 and later are fixed. Also NGINX Plus 37.0 before 37.0.8.1 and 37.1 before 37.3.0.1 (37.2.x included); older NGINX Plus R33–R36 get no fix (sources differ on R33), so move to 37.x. Distros backport fixes without changing `nginx -v`, so check the package against your distro's advisory. After upgrading, restart: a reload keeps the old binary.

affected.label: You use an affected feature
affected.text: HTTP/2 (`http2 on;` or `listen ... http2`, on any server block) is the one with a public exploit; static-only sites count, and behind a proxy that terminates HTTP/2 the exploit likely fails but the bug is still there. The same upgrade fixes bugs in HTTP/3 (`listen ... quic`) with `proxy_pass`; `resolver` with a variable in `proxy_pass` plus a `mirror` or SSI subrequest; the mail proxy with `proxy on` and `auth_http`; and HTTPS servers using TLS 1.3, where a worker can hang (CVE-2026-118899). Smaller stream and `try_files` bugs are in the bug list.

do.label: Upgrade nginx
do.text: 1.31.9 (mainline) or 1.30.7 (stable). NGINX Plus: 37.3.0.1 or 37.0.8.1. The 23 Nov releases (1.31.10, 1.30.8, NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1, 37.0.9.1) also fix a separate medium-rated CPU bug when `ssl_early_data` is on (CVE-2026-132779), so go straight to those. Debian (DSA-6642-1, DLA-4918-1) and Ubuntu (USN-9159-1, USN-9182-1) have fixed packages. Then restart.

do.label: Can't upgrade? Turn off what you can
do.text: HTTP/2: set `http2 off;` in each server block and remove `http2` from every `listen` line (before 1.25.1, only the `listen` change); this breaks native gRPC. HTTP/3: remove `quic` from `listen` and set `http3 off;`. Resolver: point `proxy_pass` at a fixed `upstream` and turn off `mirror`; Xint says turning off `mirror` alone isn't enough. Mail proxy: bind its listeners to `127.0.0.1` or firewall them. F5 gives no workaround for the TLS 1.3 hang.

do.label: Check bundled nginx
do.text: Kong, APISIX, NGINX Gateway Fabric and community ingress-nginx bundle nginx with HTTP/2 on by default. APISIX 3.21.0 and NGINX Gateway Fabric 2.9.0 are built on the fixed 1.31.9; F5's NGINX Ingress Controller 5.8.0 still ships 1.31.8. Community ingress-nginx gets no fixes after March 2026. Check with your vendor.

changes.text: Clarified: the public exploit can run code as the worker user, not only crash nginx; it gets around ASLR with addresses the bug itself leaks. Added how hard the public exploit is to use (about 128 GB of traffic, built for a fresh test server) and Xint's claim that its own exploit works on busy cloud servers. Noted the 23 Nov releases, which also fix a separate `ssl_early_data` CPU bug.

Now lists all ten CVEs fixed by the 18 Nov releases, with a bug list. "Are you affected?" covers the HTTP/3, resolver, mail proxy and TLS 1.3 bugs, not only HTTP/2. Corrected the affected NGINX Plus range (37.2.x is affected too).
Points to the Linux SCTP root page for the kernel bug Xint chained it with.
Added CVE-2026-123633 (second HTTP/2 bug, same fix) and the other nginx bugs fixed by the same releases; Debian DLA-4918-1.
APISIX 3.21.0 and NGINX Gateway Fabric 2.9.0 include the fix; NGINX Ingress Controller 5.8.0 doesn't yet. Debian and Ubuntu packages out. Safe versions added.
Review: NGINX Plus R33–R36 (no fix), full HTTP/2 workaround, ASLR note, bundled-nginx sources.
Public exploit released. No attacks seen.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 flow-control memory corruption
bugs.text: Any server with HTTP/2 on. With no login, a public exploit crashes nginx or runs code as the worker user, getting around ASLR with leaked addresses; it needs about 128 GB of traffic and is built for a freshly started test server. Versions 1.9.5–1.31.8.

bugs.title: HTTP/2 use-after-free when proxying
bugs.text: HTTP/2 plus proxying to a backend, while a worker is running low on `worker_connections`. Crash, or code execution with the same ASLR caveat. Versions 1.19.7–1.31.8.

bugs.title: HTTP/3 use-after-free
bugs.text: HTTP/3 (`listen ... quic`) with `proxy_pass`; F5 adds conditions beyond the attacker's control. Crash, or code execution with the same ASLR caveat. Turning off HTTP/2 doesn't help. Versions 1.25.0–1.31.8.

bugs.title: Resolver use-after-free
bugs.text: `resolver` with a variable in `proxy_pass` and a `mirror` or SSI subrequest to the same name. Crash, or code execution with the same ASLR caveat. Versions 0.6.18–1.31.8.

bugs.title: Mail proxy use-after-free
bugs.text: The mail proxy with `proxy on` and `auth_http`; no valid mail login needed. Crash, or code execution with the same ASLR caveat. Versions 0.5.33–1.31.8.

bugs.title: TLS 1.3 hang while reading a request body
bugs.text: Any `listen ... ssl` server in `http` that allows TLS 1.3. A worker can get stuck in a loop (denial of service), not code execution. No workaround from F5. Versions 1.13.0–1.31.8.
